cards.explanation: The answer is stay here and keep watch. Jesus says, “Stay here and keep watch.” He doesn't hand Peter, James and John a big job. I think He wants them close and awake while He carries something heavy.
The answer is True. After “Abba, Father,” Jesus says, “all things are possible for You.” Then He asks for the cup to be taken away. He's talking honestly to His Father about what's ahead.

The answer is that He wants the Father's will over His own. Jesus says, “Yet not what I will, but what You will.” The ask is real, and so is the yielding, both in one prayer. I think that's one of the most honest prayers in the whole Bible.

The answer is sleeping. Peter, James and John, three of Jesus' disciples, were asked to keep watch, and Jesus finds them asleep. He says, “Simon, are you asleep?” It's a very human moment, friends, and I've been in the same spot with a long day and a warm blanket.

The answer is so they won't enter into temptation. Jesus says, “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation.” Then He adds, “For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.” He's looking out for them.

The answer is True, and it's a kind thing to say to sleepy friends. Jesus says, “For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.” He says it right after telling them, “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation.” He names it plainly.
The answer is False. They're not awake. Jesus comes back a second time and finds them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy. The watch isn't going well, and I think we've all had a night like that.

The answer is that they don't know what to answer. Mark 14:40 says they did not know what to answer Him. I think when you've been caught napping on a job you were given, silence is the only thing you can come up with.

The answer is that He is betrayed into the hands of sinners. Jesus tells them, “Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). The hour He prayed about has come.
The answer is betrayer. Jesus says, “Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!” He tells them to rise and then points out who is coming.

The answer is swords and clubs. The crowd with Judas, one of the Twelve, comes armed with exactly that. They were sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders. Nobody brings clubs to a chat, friends.

The answer is the One he kisses. Judas tells them, “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.” Then he goes directly to Jesus, says “Rabbi!” and kisses Him. A greeting turned into a sign.
The answer is an outlaw. Jesus asks, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?” He sees what's happening and says it out loud.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me.” Every day, right out in the open. Then Judas shows up with a crowd armed with swords and clubs (Mark 14:43), and suddenly they're ready to arrest Him.

The answer is so the Scriptures would be fulfilled. Jesus says, “But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.” So what's unfolding here isn't random, friends. And the story isn't over.
The answer is False. They don't stay by His side. The text says, “Then everyone deserted Him and fled.” I think this is one of the hardest lines in the passage.
The answer is that he runs away. They caught hold of him, but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away naked. The cloth stayed behind and he kept going.
